author: DPA
title: ECB seen holding rates as Iran war fuels inflation risks - NewsBreak
text:
By DPA ,
now
The European Central Bank is not expected to raise interest rates at its meeting on Thursday, as policymakers assess the inflationary impact of rising energy prices linked to the Iran war.
Analysts broadly expect the ECB’s Governing Council to leave interest rates unchanged for now, opting to wait for clearer data on how the conflict is affecting the economy.
The deposit rate, a key benchmark for savers and banks, is likely to remain at 2%. The central bank is due to announce its decision at 2:15 pm (1215 GMT).
Rising energy costs tied to the conflict risk pushing inflation higher in the 21-member eurozone. Consumer prices rose 2.6% year-on-year in March, the strongest increase since July 2024 and above the ECB’s 2% medium-term target.
Financial markets have recently increased bets that the ECB could tighten policy later this year. While higher interest rates can help curb inflation by dampening demand, they also risk weighing on the eurozone's economic growth.
ECB President Christine Lagarde has signalled readiness to act if needed, stressing that the duration of the conflict in the Middle East will be a key factor. She has warned that higher energy prices are likely to have a significant short-term impact on inflation, while indicating that the ECB will move once it has sufficient clarity on the scale and persistence of the shock.
